Nxeon is a VPS/game-server hosting platform (Next.js 15 app, Postgres via Prisma). You must do ALL your work inside /opt/nxeon-agent-deploybtn — this is a pre-prepared git worktree on its own branch (agent-deploy-button-carry), completely separate from the main /opt/nxeon working tree which another process is actively using concurrently. Do NOT touch /opt/nxeon itself. cd into /opt/nxeon-agent-deploybtn first and stay there for everything (reads, edits, tsc, tests). node_modules and .env are already symlinked in for you. When done, commit your work there (to the existing agent-deploy-button-carry branch — do NOT create a different branch, do NOT merge to main, do NOT push, do NOT run any deploy script) and report back the summary. IMPORTANT: never run `git add -A` or `git add .` in this worktree — node_modules is a symlink and a broad add can stage it in a way that corrupts the real one elsewhere; always `git add` specific files by name.

**The problem**: across the game-servers catalog pages, the pricing page, and individual game marketing pages, there are "Deploy" buttons that currently just link to a generic pricing page/chart rather than taking the customer anywhere close to actually deploying the specific thing they clicked on. A customer who clicks "Deploy" on, say, a specific Valheim plan card has to then re-navigate a pricing chart, re-pick the game, re-pick the plan, and separately configure storage/add-ons/player-count — even though all of that context was already known from what they clicked. This is real, avoidable friction in the conversion funnel.

**The goal**: make every "Deploy" button across the site (game-servers pages, pricing page, individual per-service marketing pages) carry the FULL intended configuration — game/plan/addon selections, extra storage, player-count tier, whatever is selectable at that point — through login/signup (for a logged-out visitor) and land the customer directly in the deploy wizard (app/dashboard/deploy, or wherever it actually lives — find it) with that exact configuration PRE-FILLED, not requiring them to redo the selection.

Steps:
1. First, thoroughly investigate the current state: find every "Deploy" button/link across app/(marketing)/ and app/dashboard/deploy — where does each one currently point, and what query params/state (if any) does it already carry? Find the actual deploy wizard's page and understand what inputs/state it accepts today (does it already support ANY pre-fill via query params, e.g. a `?plan=` or `?game=` param? Check for existing partial support before assuming there's none).
2. Check how login/signup redirect currently works for a logged-out visitor clicking something that requires an account (is there an existing `?next=` or `redirect` param convention already used elsewhere in the codebase for this exact "preserve intent across auth" pattern? grep for `redirectTo`, `next=`, `callbackUrl`, etc.). Reuse whatever convention already exists rather than inventing a new one.
3. Design and implement: every relevant Deploy button/link across the marketing site should encode its specific game+plan+addon+storage+player-count selection into a URL (query params, or a short-lived server-side "intent" record if the config is too large/complex for a clean URL — pick whichever fits the existing codebase conventions best), survive the login/signup flow unchanged, and pre-populate the deploy wizard's fields on arrival so the customer can review and confirm rather than starting over.
4. Update the actual Deploy buttons on: the game-servers catalog page(s), the pricing page, and individual per-game/per-service marketing pages, to build and pass this configuration through.

Read enough of the existing deploy wizard component(s) and order/checkout flow (lib/order.ts, lib/game-order.ts, relevant app/dashboard/deploy files) to understand the real shape of a "plan selection" before designing the URL/intent schema — match the wizard's actual field names/types rather than guessing.

Before finishing: run `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx tsx --test test/*.test.ts`, and confirm your changes don't introduce new test failures beyond whatever pre-existing baseline exists (git stash your changes, run tests, compare counts, then restore). Note: a pre-existing baseline of ~35 unrelated failures (billing/pricing/auth tests) is already known and expected — don't try to fix those, just confirm your changes don't ADD to that count.

Report back with: what the URL/intent-carrying mechanism looks like, which pages were updated, and confirmation that typecheck + tests are clean (or unchanged from baseline).

## Summary

**The mechanism:** `lib/deploy-intent.ts` defines a `DeployIntent` type and `deployHref()` builder that encodes a game/plan/addon/storage/term selection onto `/dashboard/deploy?...`. It deliberately reuses the pre-existing `?product=vps|game|hosting|email` convention I found already scattered across the codebase (dashboard buttons, payment redirect/cancel paths, `GameConfigurator`, `kb-plans.ts`) rather than inventing a new name — but that convention had been silently dead since the wizard migrated from `DeployHub` (legacy, now `legacy-page.tsx.bak`) to the current `components/nx/DeployView.tsx` + `order.tsx`, which never read `useSearchParams()` at all. Other fields (`plan`, `term`, `addons`, `disk`, `family`, `tier`, `variant`, `players`, `hosting`, `email`) mirror `Order`'s own field names/types directly.

`components/nx/order.tsx` now parses that URL on mount and validates every id against the live `cat` before using it (stale/deactivated ids degrade to the normal defaults, never a broken order). Where a marketing surface only knows a target player count rather than a real `GamePlan` id (the per-game landing pages' fixture data), it maps to the nearest real tier for that family.

**Login/signup carry-through:** confirmed and reused the existing `?next=` + `safeNext()` allowlist convention (already used by `/login`, `/register`, Google/Discord OAuth). Found and fixed a real gap: `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`'s redirect for a logged-out visitor was a bare `redirect("/login")` with no `next=` at all — meaning every `/dashboard/*` deep link, including every Deploy button here, lost its destination on login for any signed-out visitor. Fixed via `middleware.ts` (added an `x-search` header alongside the existing `x-pathname` one) + `safeNext`.

**Pages/components updated:** `GameConfigurator` (game-servers catalog), `PricingExplorer` (pricing page — plan cards + VPS add-on builder), `GameLandingCombined` (all 5 CTAs, shared by 31 per-game marketing pages), `PricingGrid` (shared by `vps/page.tsx`, `ComparePageLayout`, `MigrateFromPageLayout`, and `UseCaseLanding`'s 12 pages), `VpsLanding` (also fixed two buttons that dead-linked to their own page), `UseCaseLanding`, and the two `GameLandingPage` callers (`fivem-server-hosting`, `gaming-vps`).
